# Working directory

The process's current directory, and a path made absolute or canonical against it.

<h2 id="symbolic-link-limit"><code>SymbolicLinkLimit</code></h2>

```rux
pub const SymbolicLinkLimit: uint = 40;
```

How many symbolic links one canonicalization will follow before giving up.
A link that points at itself, or at a chain that returns to it, would otherwise be followed forever. The
limit is what every system uses for the same reason, and reaching it is reported as `LimitExceeded`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Location.rux#L30)


<h2 id="set-current-directory"><code>SetCurrentDirectory</code></h2>

```rux
pub func SetCurrentDirectory(
    allocator: Allocator,
    path: Path
) -> ! IoError
```

Makes `path` the process's working directory.
Process-wide and immediately visible to every thread, which invalidates every relative path any of them was
about to resolve. Nothing in this package calls it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Location.rux#L66)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |
| `path`      | `Path`      | the path to act on           |

**Returns**: success when the working directory changed

<h2 id="absolute"><code>Absolute</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Absolute(
    allocator: Allocator,
    path: Path
) -> PathBuffer ! IoError
```

`path` made absolute against the working directory and simplified lexically.
Arithmetic, not a question for the filesystem: the path need not exist, nothing is opened, and no symbolic
link is resolved — so a `..` that crosses one is simplified away as though it did not. [`Canonicalize`](/docs/api/filesystem/location#canonicalize) is the
operation that tells the truth about links, at the cost of requiring the file to be there.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Location.rux#L90)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |
| `path`      | `Path`      | the path to act on           |

**Returns**: the path made absolute without touching the file system

<h2 id="canonicalize"><code>Canonicalize</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Canonicalize(
    allocator: Allocator,
    path: Path
) -> PathBuffer ! IoError
```

The one true name of the existing file `path` refers to.
Every symbolic link is resolved, every `.` and `..` is applied against what those links actually mean, and
the result is absolute. Unlike [`Absolute`](/docs/api/filesystem/location#absolute), the file must exist: this is a question for the filesystem, and a
name with nothing behind it has no true form. A link chain that returns to itself is `LimitExceeded` rather
than a hang.
On Windows the answer arrives in the verbatim form and spelled as the filesystem stores it — the case the
name actually has, short names expanded — because that is what the system reports, and rewriting it would be
this package guessing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/FileSystem/Src/Location.rux#L218)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from |
| `path`      | `Path`      | the path to act on           |

**Returns**: the path with every link and relative component resolved, which needs the file system and so can fail
